ov: More than 3,000 species of sap-sucking bugs with wide-set eyes and clear wings, living in trees in temperate and tropical places worldwide. Males make very loud songs by buckling drum-like tymbals. Most species appear every year, but North America's periodical cicadas emerge together every 13 or 17 years.

why.et: Eaten in various parts of the world, including China, Myanmar, Malaysia, central Africa and parts of Mexico.

len: Wingspan up to about 20 cm (Malaysian emperor cicada)
rg: Temperate to tropical regions around the world; periodical cicadas live only in North America.
df: Watery sap from the xylem of trees and other plants, sucked up through a sharp, beak-like mouthpart.
fx: Desert cicadas can cool down by sweating excess sap out through pores in their backs.
The Australian greengrocer cicada is among the loudest insects in the world.
